Below is a quick “starter kit” you can copy‑paste into your own script (or run directly from the command line) to pull **exactly seven** new comments from Reddit starting after the cursor `cursor789`.  
I’ll show both a plain `curl` one‑liner and a short Python snippet that uses the popular `requests` package – so pick whichever fits best in your workflow.

---

### 1️⃣ What you’re asking for

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Domain/API endpoint | `https://oauth.reddit.com/api/info/` (the official Reddit OAuth endpoint for comment retrieval) |
| Number of items | **7** |
| Cursor / pagination token | `cursor789` (`after=` parameter) |
| Authentication | Your bearer token: **“beta_key”** |

> ⚠️ *Reddit’s public API requires OAuth2 authentication.*  
> If you haven’t already obtained a client ID & secret, follow their [OAuth guide](https://github.com/reddit-archive/reddit/wiki/OAuth2). Once you’ve got a refresh token, exchange it for an access token and replace `"beta_key"` below with that real token.

---

### 2️⃣ One‑line `curl`

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer beta_key" \
     -H "User-Agent: my-reddit-client/0.1 by <your_redditor>" \
     "https://oauth.reddit.com/r/all/comment/search?q=&sort=new&limit=7&after=cursor789"
```

*Explanation*

- `-H "Authorization: Bearer …"` sends your OAuth token.  
- `-H "User-Agent:"` is required by Reddit; give something descriptive.  
- Query parameters:
  - `q=` – empty search query means “all”.  
  - `sort=new` – newest first.  
  - `limit=7` – exactly 7 results.  
  - `after=cursor789` – start after the given cursor.

If everything works, you’ll receive JSON containing the next page of comments plus a new `next` cursor you can feed back into subsequent calls.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Python helper

```python
import requests

API_URL   = "https://oauth.reddit.com/r/all/comment/search"
TOKEN     = "beta_key"          # <-- put your actual bearer token here
CURSOR    = "cursor789"

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "User-Agent": "my-reddit-client/0.1 by <your_redditor>"
}

params = {
    "q": "",            # blank search → all comments
    "sort": "new",
    "limit": 7,
    "after": CURSOR
}

resp = requests.get(API_URL, headers=headers, params=params)
data = resp.json()

print("Fetched {} comments".format(len(data["children"])))
for i, child in enumerate(data["children"], 1):
    print(f"{i}. [{child['kind']}] {child['data']['body'][:80]}…")

# Grab the next cursor if you plan another round
if "after" in data.get("data", {}):
    print("\nNext cursor:", data["data"]["after"])
else:
    print("\nNo more pages.")
```

#### How it works

1. Builds the same URL + query string as the `curl` example.  
2. Sends the OAuth header.  
3. Parses the returned JSON and prints out each comment body (truncated to 80 chars for brevity).  
4. Prints the next cursor value so you can loop again if needed.

---

### 4️⃣ Things to keep in mind

| Topic | Why it matters |
|-------|----------------|
| Rate limits | Reddit caps ~60 requests/minute per app/user. Keep loops polite! |
| Pagination | Use the `after` field from the response instead of hard‑coding cursors unless you know they won’t change. |
| Error handling | Check `resp.status_code`; handle 401 (token expired), 429 (rate limit exceeded), etc. |
| User‑Agent compliance | Reddit strongly recommends identifying yourself clearly—replace `<your_redditor>` with your username. |

That’s basically all you need to grab those 7 comments. Happy coding!
